Offline unread dots: guarded client candidate

Guarded, version-pinned client candidate for offline unread receipts; not installed or window-verified.

About 10 min read · 4 sections

On this page
01 Observed cause 02 Prototype boundary 03 Durable migration and wake reconciliation 04 Guarded automatic read

This is an experiment, not an installed fix. The scripts only produce renderer bytes in memory; the optional preparation script saves those assets and their original bytes under /tmp. They do not copy, modify, sign, install, or launch an application. They are not part of the gateway release package.

Observed cause

With shared gateway execution, a synthetic turn completed while the reader was disconnected. A fresh reader received the completed chat as idle and received its durable unread receipt in the top-level thread/list.readStates map. thread/read.readState agreed. The check also passed with the installed native engine handling the native list. No paid inference or production chat was used.

The desktop renderer in app version 26.1021.31345 does not consume those receipts. Its unread boolean normally changes on a live completion event, which the disconnected reader missed. Restarting the gateway cannot repair that client-side state.

Remote SDK finishes → durable unread receipt exists
Laptop reconnects  → list contains receipt
Current renderer   → ignores receipt → no blue dot
Prototype bridge   → consumes receipt → existing unread store

Sleep/wake diagnosis against the installed client

On October 28, the installed Studio and MacBook renderers both matched the exact 26.1021.31345 asset hash below. The stock list paginator (ptn in this pinned asset) appends only each reply's data rows and returns that array. It discards the accompanying readStates map. The store's getThreadHasUnreadTurn checks the saved local value first, so a saved false continues to hide attention after a completion that happened while the client was disconnected.

codex-unread-wake-diagnosis.test.mjs executes those two extracted stock functions in memory and reproduces the missing dot from a valid offline unread receipt. Wrapping that same request with the uninstalled bridge restores the stock getter without replaying a terminal or acknowledging a read. The separate stock automatic-read regression still reproduces the earlier stuck-dot race. These checks isolate the client-state failure; they do not simulate physical sleep or verify a rendered application window.

The earlier replay attempt was introduced in d5e3130, made device-specific in 0f7b6f5, and disconnected from stock resume in 93afa8c. The guarded client candidate in 5f94e85 remains uninstalled. No app, running process or receipt was changed to perform the October 28 diagnosis.

A read-only comparison also found eight of ten sampled SDK-unread chat IDs absent from the MacBook's saved Studio-host unread set. The client does not acknowledge those SDK receipts, so this mismatch can include chats already read locally; it does not prove that all eight contain unseen work. The current candidate preserves each native choice on first observation and reconciles subsequent revision changes. It cannot retrospectively classify that ambiguous, pre-installation attention.

Replaying arbitrary old completion events is not a safe substitute. The renderer has no general completion-ID deduplication before unread and notification side effects; replay could mark an already-read chat unread or repeat an alert. The gateway retains its bounded private ledger for a future explicit client contract, but stock adapters do not query for or replay a historical terminal on resume. Passive gateway observers remain status-only, and offline completion therefore does not currently guarantee a stock unread dot.

Prototype boundary

scripts/codex-unread-trial/patch.mjs locates the manager and notification dispatcher structurally. Its paired entry point requires the exact app version and both renderer and conversation-chunk SHA-256 hashes. Missing, changed, ambiguous, or already-patched hooks are rejected. Tests execute independent fixtures and the extracted, patched stock automatic-read function in a simulated native scope. This is not execution in an actual application window.

The bridge imports SDK receipts into both the existing unread store and the manager's loaded-row state. It acknowledges the manager's semantic read/unread actions using the receipt's opaque revision; ordinary cache and terminal store writes never send an acknowledgement. It serializes newer actions and rejects stale snapshots without blindly retrying a read conflict. Each metadata map retains at most 200 threads. Eviction conservatively rejects old in-flight snapshots until a later refresh. Missing or malformed receipts retain legacy behavior. It does not invent turns, execute tools, or change inference or permissions.

Durable migration and wake reconciliation

The paired candidate journals receipt revisions in IndexedDB. Its scope is a SHA-256 hash of the native durable account identity and execution-host token, obtained through the native facade's own lifecycle guard. Host display names and random manager generations are never persistence identities. The account-unaware legacy facade, missing WebCrypto/IndexedDB, storage failure, or a retired scope leaves the native behavior in place.

Observation Local projection
First receipt for an existing chat Preserve the native read/unread choice; save its revision without sending an ACK.
Same revision after reload or wake Use the saved projection.
Later SDK revision Reconcile its unread state, including completions missed while disconnected.
Successful durable start/fork Register a fresh chat so its first completion is not treated as legacy history.
Semantic read/unread already satisfied by the SDK Persist the explicit local choice without an unnecessary SDK mutation.

Migration limit: the native ready facade returns false for any ID absent from its unread set, including a chat it has never seen. SDK unread alone cannot distinguish a previously read chat from a new chat created elsewhere. A first-seen chat created on another device therefore also keeps that native choice; its next receipt revision reconciles normally. Only a start/fork response witnessed by this client establishes a safe fresh baseline. A complete cross-device rollout needs an explicit initial catalog/migration contract; this candidate does not guess creation times or claim to repair that ambiguity.

Each scope retains up to 10,000 chat checkpoints. Capacity failure preserves native behavior instead of evicting unseen attention. Successful deletes remove the chat's checkpoint. Rows contain only a scope hash, chat ID, opaque revision, boolean, and journal sequence; account identities and message content are not stored in this database.

A shared transactional sequence is captured before metadata requests. A delayed reply cannot replace a newer checkpoint written by another window. Push events request fresh metadata rather than trusting their arrival order. Local action generations abort pending IndexedDB projections that race with a read/unread action, including their disk writes. Failed explicit no-op choices remain bound to their captured revision until a later action or refresh retries them. They never retarget a read onto newer attention. Persistence operations have a two-second deadline and cannot fail the caller's successful SDK response. Historical completion events are never replayed.

Guarded automatic read

The stock hook deduplicates reads by request ID, last turn ID/status, and a native signal. An offline receipt can arrive after that hook already ran. Replaying completion events can restore the dot without changing those dedup keys. Merely adding the receipt revision is unsafe too: first unread can remain A while a newer, unseen B changes the revision.

The paired candidate requires a stable receipt, a matching latest terminal turn with fully loaded items, and a still-focused, mounted chat on the same host before invoking the stock semantic read. Its acknowledgement uses the captured revision, never a blindly retargeted conflict revision. Every newer SDK attention publication changes that revision, even if first unread stays the same (publish_thread_attention in the pinned SDK state runtime).

Capture receipt R + action/history generations
  → query latest SDK turn
  → await native loaded-history capability; copy ID/status/completeness; dispose it
  → metadata-only thread/read must still report R
  → recheck generations, focus, mounted chat, host, and matching terminal history
  → call stock semantic read without another await → CAS acknowledgement of R

When no valid receipt is known, the original local-only read behavior remains. An unknown-revision read never queues a durable acknowledgement. A later receipt can restore attention and trigger guarded reconciliation.

Native history invalidation (K2n, keyed by conversation ID in this pinned renderer) and receipt subscriptions permit retry after hydration. Failed proofs do not consume a revision. The hook coalesces evaluations, retires probes on unmount, and expires their commit authority after five seconds. Raw validation RPCs do not ingest receipts or invalidate their own action epoch. Old same-host managers are disposed before installing successor wrappers.

Manual unread before the first receipt remains pending and requests metadata for its CAS. It must become threadStart; an existing turn-based unread receipt does not satisfy manual intent. Transport failure retains that intent until a later refresh or explicit action retries it.

The native latest turn retains its item-pagination proof even when older thread pages are absent. The candidate accepts that turn only when its oldest item page is loaded, its older cursor is exhausted, and it is neither loading, evicted, nor reconnecting. The latest SDK turn ID/status must still match. This permits a read in a long chat without fetching every older turn. Missing or partial latest items retain the dot. Selection, summary metadata, or thread/resume alone never prove reading. Native-window lifecycle verification remains required.

Prepare paired assets and a rollback manifest without touching an app:

node scripts/codex-unread-trial/prepare.mjs /Applications/ChatGPT.app

The printed /tmp/hg-unread-candidate-*/manifest.json records source and asset hashes, checkpoint migration/scoping, and the uninstalled/unverified status. An app update invalidates the pins and refuses preparation. Rollback from an authorized trial is to discard its disposable app copy; the original signed application remains unchanged.

An actual window test is still required before claiming the blue dot works. Applying the prototype to a disposable ChatGPT/Codex app copy would require explicit authorization for that app's signing and identity changes. Prior Claude trial authorization does not authorize modifying ChatGPT. The installed application must remain untouched without that authorization.

Run the isolated regression tests with:

node --test scripts/claude-desktop-tests/codex-unread-*.test.mjs \
  scripts/claude-desktop-tests/codex-read-state-bridge.test.mjs

Run the real-IndexedDB checks with abx installed:

node scripts/codex-unread-trial/verify-checkpoints.mjs

This creates its own localhost origin and isolated BROWSE_STATE_FILE under /tmp/hg-checkpoint-browser-*, then stops only that browser daemon. It does not connect to ChatGPT or the gateway. Checks cover first-sync choices, new chats, semantic read persistence, account/host isolation, retired scopes, capacity and storage errors, document reload, and stale/concurrent replies from separate same-origin documents with real IndexedDB connections. Its report.json records only synthetic test results. These checks do not reproduce physical Mac sleep or verify the installed app's rendered dot, and they do not change the mobile client.

The existing synthetic chat-state fixture also has an optional --unread check. It acknowledges an initial receipt, disconnects the reader, completes another turn, reconnects, and checks both restored unread state and an explicit durable read acknowledgement. It also rejects a guarded read from the older transcript before allowing a matching hydrated view. It asserts that no completion was replayed and that a later refresh stays read. Its store and loaded-history view are synthetic facades, so this still does not verify a native window dot.

node scripts/e2e-chat-state.mjs --package /path/to/verified/package \
  --root /tmp/task-specific-evidence --unread \
  --native-engine /path/to/original/native/codex

--native-engine changes only the fixture's native-side engine. The verified gateway SDK still owns gateway inference. All chat homes, synthetic responses, and gateway configuration remain isolated under /tmp.

On October 25, 2026, the earlier isolated check passed with the original installed native engine and the verified gateway SDK: three synthetic turns, zero paid inference, offline receipt imported, explicit read persisted, subsequent refresh stayed read, and zero replayed terminal events. The 23 focused bridge, structural-hook, and race checks also passed. These are protocol and synthetic client checks, not evidence of a working dot in the installed window.

The final source check, build, and full test suites passed on an isolated snapshot containing only this experiment: 3,327 core tests and 116 desktop tests passed, with two optional skips. Unrelated in-progress API-mode changes in the shared checkout were excluded from that snapshot. Those results describe the earlier prototype, not this candidate's native-window readiness.

On October 26, 2026, the guarded real-SDK fixture passed with three synthetic turns and zero paid requests: offline receipt restored, older transcript refused, matching hydrated view acknowledged durably, refresh stayed read, and zero replayed completions. Regressions also cover unchanged-first-unread supersession, pending manual unread, stale manager overlap, invalidated proofs, and close/reopen of the same chat. The build and type check passed; 3,485 core tests and 144 desktop tests passed, with two optional skips and no failures. Native-window verification remains pending.

On October 28, 2026, the migration/checkpoint candidate passed build, type check, 3,557 core tests and 160 desktop tests, with two optional skips and no failures. Ten real-browser IndexedDB checks passed, including transaction rollback after a semantic read during first-sync writes, separate-document concurrency and reload. Independent review found and verified corrections for the first-sync disk race, failed/duplicate no-op choices, and stale cross-window choice revisions. The real-SDK fixture also passed with three synthetic requests, zero paid inference, and zero replayed completions; that protocol fixture uses a synthetic store and does not exercise IndexedDB. The candidate remains local and uninstalled. Mobile, physical sleep/wake, and native-window verification remain outside this evidence.
